witness_description: Let J={j_n:n>=0}, take v_{j_0}=1 and v_{j_n}=0 for every n>=1, and take r=1.
refutation_explanation: This family has finite support, so it is absolutely summable. Its generalized sum over J is 1, hence converges absolutely to r=1. The series starting at n=1 contains only zero terms and therefore converges absolutely to 0, not to r=1. Thus the stated equivalence fails because it omits v_{j_0}.
search_space: Exhaustively swept all 729 pairs consisting of r in (1,0,-1,2,-2,3,-3,4,-4) and a family on J={j_n:n>=0} with each of v_{j_0},...,v_{j_3} in (0,1,-1) and v_{j_n}=0 for every n>=4.
